title: Checkout risk gate with fraud-scoring fallback
name: Checkout risk gate

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code behaves when the fraud-scoring service is unavailable? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: Only ScoringTimeoutError triggers the fallback. When the scoring service is down outright (connection refused, DNS failure) or returns a 5xx, the client throws a plain Error, which evaluate rethrows. Every checkout then fails instead of using the fallback policy, so a scoring outage becomes a payments outage. Unavailability errors (network errors and 5xx) should route to fallback too; only genuine client errors should propagate.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Scoring times out for a charge above fallbackAutoApproveMaxCents. What happens?
choices: The charge is approved with score null
The payment is enqueued for review and the decision is "review"
evaluate throws ScoringTimeoutError to the caller
choiceQuestions.explanation: The timeout is converted to ScoringTimeoutError and handled by fallback(). For amounts above the auto-approve cap, fallback enqueues a review and returns "review". Small amounts are approved; nothing in fallback declines; the error is not rethrown.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is the purpose of passing controller.signal to the scoring client?
choices: It lets the client retry automatically on abort
It cancels the in-flight HTTP request when the deadline passes, rather than leaving it running
It ensures the review queue message is deduplicated
It makes the score request idempotent
choiceQuestions.explanation: The timer calls controller.abort(), and fetch honours the signal by cancelling the request, so slow calls do not pile up sockets. The client has no retry logic, and the signal has nothing to do with dedupe or idempotency.

choices: Accepting some unscored fraud risk on small charges to keep checkout working, while routing larger ones to human review
Reducing load on the scoring service by skipping it for small charges
Lowering latency for every charge by caching scores
Rejecting large charges to protect the merchant during outages
choiceQuestions.explanation: The cap is only consulted in fallback(), i.e. when no score is available: small charges are approved unscored, larger ones go to review. Scoring is always attempted first, there is no cache, and large charges are reviewed, not rejected.
